title: Equivariant lisse extension on the full parameter-root tower
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a norm-topological finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ containing $E$ with the extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for every profinite set $P$, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], ordinary unbounded derived categories and total derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme with a finite reduced strict normal crossings divisor $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Put $W=Y\setminus D$, and let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Assume that on every strict henselization the pullback of $L$ to the complement becomes constant after adjoining compatible roots of all boundary parameters of all positive orders prime to $p$; strict henselization is [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Fix $I\subseteq A$ and the reduced stratum $S_I=(\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i)\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin I}D_a$.
There are affine etale charts $V\to Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin I}D_a$ with equations $t_i$ for $D_i$, affine pro-etale maps $U_\alpha\to V$, and $S_\alpha=U_\alpha\times_Y S_I$, such that the $S_\alpha\to S_I$ cover in the pro-etale topology. Put
$$T_\alpha=\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}_{U_\alpha}\bigl(\mathcal O_{U_\alpha}[x_i]_{i\in I}/(x_i^n-t_i)_{i\in I}\bigr),\qquad T_\alpha^\circ=T_\alpha\times_YW.$$
Transitions are the power maps for divisibility. There are compatible primitive roots of unity on $U_\alpha$ of all orders prime to $p$, identifying the deck group with $G_I=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^I$. The map $T_\alpha^\circ\to U_\alpha^\circ=U_\alpha\times_YW$ is a pro-etale cover and a $G_I$-torsor: $(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx)$ identifies $T_\alpha^\circ[G_I]$ with $T_\alpha^\circ\times_{U_\alpha^\circ}T_\alpha^\circ$, where profinite products mean inverse limits of finite disjoint unions [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. There is a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,T_\alpha}$-module $\widetilde L_\alpha$ with continuous $G_I$-equivariant structure whose restriction to $T_\alpha^\circ$ is the actual deck-equivariant pullback of $L$. The map $i_\alpha:S_\alpha\to T_\alpha$ sets every root to zero. For some finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $M_\alpha$ there is a $G_I$-equivariant identification
$$i_\alpha^*\widetilde L_\alpha\cong p_{S_\alpha}^*(P\mapsto C(P,M_\alpha)),$$
whose action is induced by a continuous $E$-linear representation $G_I\to\operatorname{GL}_E(M_\alpha)$. The constructions restrict along refinements of this family. For $I=\varnothing$ the root tower and group are the identity and the trivial group, and this is a pro-etale trivialization of $L$. No assertion about higher direct images is included.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-snc-universal-residual-charts] to cover the stratum by its connected residual charts $V,U,S_U,T,T^\circ$, with compatible primitive roots and the specified power transitions. Its strict-local connectedness assertion verifies the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-tame-integral-reduction-family]. That lemma supplies $N$, its normalized quotients $F_n$, completeness, and their finite tameness on every relevant strict-local tower.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary extension expansion; assembly after 2026-10-22 work-spreading re-split.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-snc-tame-finite-fibre-classification] to all $F_n$ on this same universal residual chart. Naturality, products and reduction give finite free fibres $Q_n$, compatible quotient maps and trivializations with the actual deck descent actions. Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-adic-fibre-realization] with $B=U^\circ$, $X=T^\circ$ and $N|_{U^\circ}$. Obtain $Q$, $M=E\otimes_AQ$, continuous $\rho$, and the actual equivariant identification $L|_{T^\circ}\cong p_{T^\circ}^*C(-,M)$. No arbitrary inverse image is assumed to preserve infinite limits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-full-root-rotation-torsor] to $H$ and the chart parameters. Its comparison is $(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx)$ with the actual residue and power maps; combined with the chart lemma's pro-etale covering this gives the required torsor. The same lemma gives the fixed map $i:S_U\to T$ sending every root to zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary extension expansion; assembly after 2026-10-22 work-spreading re-split.

proof.text: Set $\widetilde L=p_T^*C(-,M)$. A finite basis of $M$ identifies this with $C_{E,T}^d$, hence it is lisse. Root rotations and $\rho$ give its equivariant structure, with cocycle identity $\rho(gh)=\rho(g)\rho(h)$. Step 2 identifies its open restriction with the actual pullback of $L$. Since $i$ is fixed, composition of pullback from the point identifies $i^*\widetilde L$ with $p_{S_U}^*C(-,M)$ carrying the same representation.

proof.text: The residual-chart and finite-fibre lemmas give pointed refinement maps commuting with roots, finite fibres, quotient maps and actions. The naturality clause of equivariant adic realization makes $M$, $\rho$ and the open identification compatible with them. Pulling back the finite basis and the formula $v\mapsto\rho(g)v$ identifies the constant extensions and their boundary restrictions. Compatible basis changes conjugate every finite matrix and its limit, yielding isomorphic extensions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary extension expansion; assembly after 2026-10-22 work-spreading re-split.

proof.text: For $I=\varnothing$ the chart and root-rotation lemmas give $T=U$, $G=1$ and $i=\mathrm{id}$. Finite classification and adic realization then trivialize $L|_U$. Rank zero gives $Q_n=Q=M=\widetilde L=0$; ranks may vary between charts. Empty strata use the empty family, including empty $Y$; empty divisors are the same zero-parameter case.
